**`npm publish --dry-run` packs but never authenticates — publish.yml's rehearsal claimed a credential gate it does not provide**

**What**: Run 32138680828 (after #725's fix landed) reached the publish step and failed E403: *"Two-factor authentication or granular access token with bypass 2fa enabled is required to publish packages."* The `Rehearse the publish` step (`npm publish --dry-run --access public`) passed immediately before it. Filed as **#727** (`status:needs-review`).

**The measured falsehood**: `publish.yml`'s comment says *"A rehearsal turns that into a red step before anything is uploaded, instead of an auth error half-way."* The rehearsal was green and the auth error arrived at the real publish anyway.

**Why**: `npm publish --dry-run` output is entirely local packing — file list, sizes, integrity hash, 477-file count. It answers *"what would this tarball contain?"*, never *"may this credential publish it?"*. So the workflow has **no pre-upload credential check at all**, and the first thing that ever tests `NPM_BRAIN_TOKEN` is the irreversible act itself — the exact ordering the rest of the workflow was built to avoid (version guard, manifest match and suite all refuse cheaply first).

**The pattern, with polarity inverted**: usually this repo finds a check that cannot report WHY it failed. Here a check reports SUCCESS on a question it never asked, and the reader takes that silence for coverage.

**Nothing was published.** `@logikas/brain` still 404s; E403 means the PUT was rejected.

**The token fix (maintainer, npmjs.com, part of #435 not #727)**: the account requires 2FA for publishing. Either a **classic Automation token** (bypasses 2FA by design) or a **Granular Access Token created with "bypass 2FA" enabled**. Scope it to the `@logikas` SCOPE, not to selected packages — `@logikas/brain` does not exist until the first publish, so there is nothing to select. That half of the workflow's comment is correct.

**Sequencing note**: two consecutive defects in the same workflow ([[discovery/publish-yml-npm-ci-cannot-run]] then this one) were both invisible for the same reason — it had never run. Each fix only exposes the next, because a workflow at 0 runs has had none of its steps evaluated.

**Related**: [[discovery/publish-yml-npm-ci-cannot-run]], [[sdd/issue-717-handoff-refresh/apply-progress]].
